136	## Evidence Workflow
137	
138	The benchmark evidence pipeline is:
139	
140	1. Run a benchmark job and keep the raw artifacts in `benchmark-results/`.
141	2. Import the resulting run, report, or curated snapshot into JSONL evidence.
142	3. Validate the imported evidence and append it to an append-only ledger.
143	4. Generate benchmark-specific or cross-benchmark claims from the ledger.
144	
145	The canonical operator loop for a TerminalBench matrix is:
146	
147	```bash
148	# 1) produce raw matrix artifacts
149	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... \
150	  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
151	
152	# 2) project raw matrix artifacts into normalized evidence
153	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench --matrix <matrix-dir> --out benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl
154	
155	# 3) validate and append to the ledger
156	go run ./cmd/bench evidence validate benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl
157	go run ./cmd/bench evidence append --in benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl
158	
159	# 4) emit benchmark claims from the ledger
160	go run ./cmd/bench fhi delta --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl --left <record_id> --right <record_id>
161	go run ./cmd/bench fhi rank --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl
162	```
163	
164	This workflow is anchored by [SD-012](../../docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-012-benchmark-evidence-ledger.md)
165	and the benchmark resource notes for
166	[Rapid-MLX MHI](../../docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md),
167	[SkillsBench](../../docs/resources/skillsbench-2026-05-06.md),
168	[SWE-bench](../../docs/resources/swebench-2026-05-06.md), and
169	[HumanEval](../../docs/resources/humaneval-2026-05-06.md).
170	
171	Beadbench enters the same ledger path through `evidence import-beadbench` from
172	its `report.json` output, and curated external snapshots enter through
173	`evidence import-external`. For a concrete beadbench source-run example, see
174	[the OMLX Qwen reasoning sweep note](../../docs/research/beadbench-omlx-qwen-reasoning-sweep-2026-04-24.md).
175	
176	Use the command family below for the full evidence loop:
177	
178	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench`
179	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-beadbench`
180	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-external`
181	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence validate`
182	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence append`
183	- `go run ./cmd/bench fhi delta`
184	- `go run ./cmd/bench fhi rank`

186	### 1. Run benchmark jobs
187	
188	Use the TerminalBench runners to produce the raw matrix or report artifacts:
189	
190	```bash
191	# Harness comparison matrix
192	BASELINE=local TIER=wide REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
193	  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
194

201	```

204	gitignored. Large logs, model outputs, tarballs, and upstream artifacts belong
205	there, not in git.
206	
207	### 2. Import benchmark evidence
208	
209	Project the source artifacts into normalized JSONL evidence with the bench CLI:
210	
211	```bash
212	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench \
213	  --matrix cmd/bench/testdata/terminalbench-matrix \
214	  --out benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl
215	
216	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-beadbench \
217	  --report cmd/bench/testdata/beadbench-report/report.json \
218	  --out benchmark-results/evidence/beadbench.jsonl
219	
220	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-external \
221	  --source cmd/bench/testdata/external-benchmarks/rapid-mlx-mhi.md \
222	  --out benchmark-results/evidence/external.jsonl
223	```
224	
225	`import-terminalbench` is the path for Harbor matrix outputs, `import-beadbench`
226	is the path for beadbench `report.json`, and `import-external` is the path for
227	curated external benchmark snapshots, including Rapid-MLX MHI, SkillsBench,
228	SWE-bench, and HumanEval fixtures. Beadbench and other local runs enter the
229	ledger through their importer paths, not by hand-editing the schema.
230	
231	Raw benchmark artifacts remain in the gitignored `benchmark-results/` tree.
232	Only curated snapshots or source hashes that have been normalized into ledger
233	records should be committed. This repo currently keeps importer fixtures in
234	`cmd/bench/testdata/external-benchmarks/` and `cmd/bench/testdata/fhi/`.
235	Approved checked-in curated snapshots, if added later, should live under
236	`scripts/benchmark/evidence/<snapshot-id>.jsonl`.

238	### 3. Validate and append to the ledger
239	
240	```bash
241	go run ./cmd/bench evidence validate benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl

248	source URLs together. Checked-in curated snapshots, when approved, live under

253	### 4. Generate FHI claims
254	
255	Use `go run ./cmd/bench fhi delta` for pairwise benchmark claims and

258	```bash

261	  --left terminalbench-delta-left-opus-claude-code \

263

269	
270	- `fhi delta` compares only two records on the same benchmark axis. Keep the
271	  benchmark, subset, scorer, formula version, and denominator policy fixed;
272	  vary only the subject axis you are measuring.
273	- `fhi rank` compares subjects across the same evidence window and formula.

419	## Vidar Qwen3.6 Harness Matrix
420	
421	`run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh` runs the shared Vidar oMLX
422	OpenAI-compatible profile against `fiz`, `pi`, and `opencode` through Harbor.
423	Use this path when comparing harness capability on the same local model/provider.
424	
425	Before running, make sure the local model endpoint is reachable from Harbor task
426	containers as `http://vidar:1235/v1`. The script sets `OMLX_API_KEY=local` by

428	
429	The `benchmark-results/` tree is ignored by git, so the pinned in-container
430	artifacts must be staged locally before a run. Defaults are:
431	
432	- `benchmark-results/bin/opencode-1.3.17-linux-x64/opencode`
433	- `benchmark-results/bin/node-v20.19.2-linux-x64.tar.gz`
434	- `benchmark-results/bin/pi-coding-agent-0.67.1/package.tgz`

443

568	
569	### Bootstrap Subset Selection
570	
571	`TIER=wide` should not rely on a hand-maintained sense of task difficulty. Use
572	the selector below to bootstrap a 15-task subset from public
573	Terminal-Bench-2 leaderboard trial rewards:
574	
575	```bash
576	scripts/benchmark/select_terminalbench_subset.py
577	```
578	
579	The selector reads reward files from
580	`harborframework/terminal-bench-2-leaderboard` on Hugging Face, groups
581	submissions into broad `frontier`, `medium_frontier`, and `non_frontier`
582	families by Fizeau catalog power, and emits:
583	
584	- tasks almost everyone passes
585	- tasks almost nobody passes
586	- tasks mostly passed by frontier submissions
587	- tasks mostly passed by medium-frontier submissions
588	- tasks consistently passed by non-frontier submissions
589	- probes where the monotonic difficulty assumption appears false
590	
591	The generated manifest is written to
592	`scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-external-bootstrap.json`. Review
593	the monotonicity report before replacing the committed `wide` subset.
594	
595	Submission directories are interpreted as `Harness__Model` when that delimiter
596	is present. The `Model` field is matched against
597	`internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` first, using the same broad display
598	variant behavior as catalog model eligibility. Leaderboard-only models that are
599	not yet in the catalog are assigned bootstrap powers in
600	`scripts/benchmark/terminalbench_model_power.json`; exact submission-name
601	overrides use a `submission:` prefix for rows that do not expose a clean
602	`Harness__Model` split or represent a multi-model stack.
603	
604	### Benchmark Evidence
605	
606	Benchmark runner outputs are benchmark-specific, but long-term model power
607	should be derived from normalized raw evidence keyed by model, harness,
608	provider, and benchmark. New importers should project source reports into the
609	schema at `scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json`; see
610	`docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-012-benchmark-evidence-ledger.md`.
611	The relevant command surface is `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench`,
612	`go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-beadbench`, `go run ./cmd/bench evidence
613	import-external`, `go run ./cmd/bench evidence append`, and `go run ./cmd/bench
614	fhi delta|rank`.
615	
616	Curated external snapshots can be imported with:
617	
618	```bash
619	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-external \
620	  --source cmd/bench/testdata/external-benchmarks/rapid-mlx-mhi.md \
621	  --out /tmp/rapid-mlx.jsonl
622	```
623	
624	The same command accepts SkillsBench CSV, SWE-bench CSV, and HumanEval JSONL
625	fixtures. Imported rows keep `unknown` harness/provider values explicit instead
626	of dropping them, and HumanEval rows are flagged as low-cost model-power
627	evidence rather than primary FHI coverage.
628	
629	### Claude and Codex reference baselines
630	
631	Set `BASELINE=frontier` to run native Claude Code and Codex reference cells:
632	
633	```bash
634	BASELINE=frontier TIER=canary REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
635	  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
636	```
637	
638	These cells are **not model-controlled comparisons** against Vidar/Qwen. They
639	answer a different question: how the native subscription/reference harnesses
640	perform on the same TerminalBench tasks. Keep them in a separate table from the
641	local-model rows unless the analysis explicitly calls out the model confound.
642	
643	The runner uses paired one-cell invocations so Claude Code only runs with
644	`claude-native-sonnet-4-6` (`sonnet-4.6`) and Codex only runs with
645	`codex-native-gpt-5-4-mini` (`gpt-5.4-mini`). This avoids meaningless
646	cross-products like Claude Code with the Codex profile.
647	
648	Prepare linux artifacts before running inside Harbor containers:
649	
650	```bash
651	scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
652	```
653	
654	The runner prepares native Claude/Codex harness artifacts automatically. Harbor
655	Docker jobs are assumed to run on the host architecture by default, so the
656	runner builds `fiz` for the host `GOARCH`, looks for native CLI artifacts under
657	`benchmark-results/bin/claude-linux-<goarch>/claude` and
658	`benchmark-results/bin/codex-linux-<goarch>/codex`, and otherwise uses the
659	locally installed `claude` / `codex` binaries when they match the container
660	architecture. If a non-native container platform is forced, set
661	`HARBOR_NODE_ARCH=x64` or `HARBOR_NODE_ARCH=arm64` and the runner will instead
662	`npm pack` the matching CLI packages, upload the corresponding Node.js tarball,
663	and install the CLIs inside the Harbor container. If API key environment
664	variables are not present, it also packages local `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`
665	auth/config state into gitignored tarballs under
666	`benchmark-results/bin/native-homes/` so the container can use the same logged-in
667	CLI accounts. Set `HARBOR_SKIP_NATIVE_HOME=1` to disable that behavior.
668	
669	Manual overrides remain available:
670	
671	```bash
672	HARBOR_CLAUDE_ARTIFACT=/path/to/claude \
673	HARBOR_CODEX_ARTIFACT=/path/to/codex \
674	  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
675	```
676	
677	Authentication can use API keys passed by the profile env vars
678	(`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or a tarred harness home directory:
679	
680	```bash
681	tar -C "$HOME" -czf benchmark-results/bin/claude-home.tgz .claude
682	tar -C "$HOME" -czf benchmark-results/bin/codex-home.tgz .codex
683	
684	HARBOR_CLAUDE_HOME_TARBALL=benchmark-results/bin/claude-home.tgz \
685	HARBOR_CODEX_HOME_TARBALL=benchmark-results/bin/codex-home.tgz \
686	BASELINE=frontier TIER=canary REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
687	  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
688	```
689	
690	Do not commit those tarballs or benchmark-result artifacts.
691	
692	To compare `fiz` against the same medium-cost model families through
693	OpenRouter, run separate `fiz` cells with the official OpenRouter profiles:
694	
695	```bash
696	TIER=canary HARNESSES=fiz PROFILE=fiz-openrouter-gpt-5-4-mini REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
697	  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
698	
699	TIER=canary HARNESSES=fiz PROFILE=fiz-openrouter-claude-sonnet-4-6 REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
700	  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
701	```
702	
703	---
704	
705	## Harbor Adapter
706	
707	`harbor_agent.py` is the `BaseInstalledAgent` Python adapter that Harbor uses
708	to install and run fiz inside each task container. It handles:
709	
710	1. **`install()`** — copies the `linux/amd64` binary and writes a provider config
711	2. **`run()`** — invokes `fiz --json --preset benchmark -p "<task>"`
712	3. **`populate_context_post_run()`** — converts session JSONL to ATIF v1.4 trajectory
713	
714	The adapter's provider and prompt behavior are controlled by benchmark env vars
715	supplied by the runner, including:
716	
717	- `FIZEAU_PROVIDER_NAME`
718	- `FIZEAU_PROVIDER`
719	- `FIZEAU_MODEL`
720	- `FIZEAU_BASE_URL`
721	- `FIZEAU_API_KEY_ENV`
722	- `FIZEAU_HEADERS_JSON`
723	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_PRESET`
724	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_SYSTEM_APPEND`
725	
726	**Build the linux/amd64 binary before running**:
727	
728	```bash
729	GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o scripts/benchmark/fiz-linux-amd64 ./cmd/fiz
730	```
731	
732	### Credential injection
733	
734	The adapter passes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the host
735	into the container via `get_env()`. A minimal config file is written during
736	`install()` that references `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}` — fiz's config loader
737	expands env vars at load time.
738	
739	If the expected key env var is unset, the benchmark scripts now fall back to the
740	matching provider entry in the host fiz config (`.fizeau/config.yaml` or
741	`~/.config/fizeau/config.yaml`) and export the discovered `api_key` before
742	invoking Harbor.

9	# Solution Design: SD-012 — Benchmark Evidence Ledger and Derived Model Power
10	
11	## Summary
12	
13	Fizeau should treat benchmark observations as raw evidence, not as direct
14	catalog truth. Every benchmark runner should be able to emit normalized records
15	keyed by:
16	
17	- model
18	- harness
19	- provider
20	- benchmark
21	- benchmark task or subset
22	- run environment and scoring metadata
23	
24	Catalog `power` then becomes a derived projection over those records plus
25	cost, availability, recency, deployment class, and explicit override policy.
26	This preserves the distinction between model capability and model × harness ×
27	provider compatibility while still letting benchmark performance drive routing
28	strength over time.
29	
30	## Problem
31	
32	TerminalBench, MHI-style evals, SkillsBench, SWE-bench, HumanEval, MMLU,
33	TAU-bench, and project-local beadbench results all measure different things.
34	The concrete MHI source captured for this design is Rapid-MLX's Model-Harness
35	Index resource in `docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md`; SkillsBench,
36	SWE-bench, and HumanEval are captured in sibling files under `docs/resources/`.
37	Some benchmarks are close to model-only capability. Others are explicitly model
38	× harness behavior. Current Fizeau catalog power stores a single integer with
39	provenance, but the raw evidence that led to the integer is not represented in a
40	common shape.
41	
42	Without a raw evidence layer:
43	
44	- TerminalBench leaderboard rows can be misread as model-only scores even when
45	  the row is really `Harness__Model`.
46	- Harness effects such as tool-call parsing, prompt discipline, retry behavior,
47	  and session logging get folded into model power without attribution.
48	- Cost, speed, quota, and availability signals are mixed with capability
49	  judgments in ad hoc ways.
50	- Recomputing model power after new benchmark runs requires reconstructing
51	  intent from benchmark-specific report files.
52	
53	## Decision
54	
55	Introduce a benchmark evidence ledger format. Existing benchmark-specific
56	outputs remain the source artifacts, but importers can project them into a
57	shared JSONL record type described by
58	`scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json`.
59	
60	The ledger is append-only evidence. It does not directly change routing.
61	Catalog generation or catalog-refresh tooling reads the ledger and computes
62	model-level derived power plus model × harness capability summaries.
63	
64	## Record Identity
65	
66	A single evidence record represents one aggregate or one atomic trial. Atomic
67	task-level records are preferred when available; aggregate records are allowed
68	when the upstream source only publishes aggregate scores.
69	
70	Identity fields:
71	
72	- `schema_version`: evidence schema version.
73	- `record_id`: stable content-derived identifier.
74	- `captured_at`: when Fizeau captured/imported the record.
75	- `source`: source runner or external publisher.
76	- `benchmark`: benchmark identity and version.
77	- `subject`: model, harness, provider, endpoint, and optional surface.
78	- `scope`: task, subset, split, repetition, and run identifiers.
79	
80	Versioned identity is required for evidence that may feed FHI, catalog power,
81	or comparative claims. Records must capture, directly or through provenance:
82	
83	- Fizeau version and git commit.
84	- Harness wrapper name/version and wrapped harness CLI/runtime version.
85	- Provider name, endpoint/API surface, deployment class, and provider version or
86	  capture timestamp.
87	- Model raw name, canonical catalog id when known, resolved snapshot/version
88	  when available, quantization/precision for local artifacts, and context limit.
89	- Benchmark name/version, scorer version, dataset commit, subset id/version, and
90	  runner/importer version.
91	- Local/self-hosted runtime version, model artifact id/checksum, OS/architecture,
92	  hardware class, accelerator backend, and utilization/capacity signals when
93	  available.
94	
95	## Subject Semantics
96	
97	`subject.model` is the canonical model identity if known. `subject.model_raw`
98	preserves the model string from the source. `subject.harness` and
99	`subject.provider` are never optional for agentic/tool benchmarks; if a public
100	source hides either value, it must be recorded as `unknown`, not omitted.
101	
102	This prevents the common mistake of treating `ClaudeCode__GLM-4.7` as a GLM-only
103	score. It is a score for GLM-4.7 through Claude Code, on whatever provider and
104	version the source used.
105	
106	## Score Semantics
107	
108	The normalized `score` block carries the headline metric in a common form:
109	
110	- `metric`: e.g. `pass_rate`, `reward_mean`, `accuracy`, `mhi`.
111	- `value`: normalized 0..1 score when possible.
112	- `raw_value`: original score if different, e.g. `92` for MHI on a 0..100 scale.
113	- `n`: number of trials or tasks represented.
114	- `passed`: count of passed trials when applicable.
115	- `failed`: count of failed trials when applicable.
116	
117	Additional benchmark-specific dimensions live under `components`; examples:
118	`tool_call_success`, `terminalbench_pass_rate`, `humaneval_pass_rate`,
119	`mmlu_accuracy`, `median_wall_seconds`, `tool_calls_per_success`, and
120	`cost_per_success_usd`.
121	
122	## Derived Power
123	
124	Catalog `models.yaml` remains the compact routing surface. `power` is derived
125	from evidence, but the derivation is intentionally policy-owned:
126	
127	1. Normalize each benchmark into capability dimensions.
128	2. Separate model-only evidence from model × harness evidence.
129	3. Weight reliable, harness-normalized agentic benchmarks heavily for coding
130	   agent routing. TerminalBench should become a major contributor once we have
131	   harness-normalized rows.
132	4. Apply deployment-class and availability guardrails. A local/community model
133	   should not receive managed-cloud frontier power from one benchmark alone.
134	5. Apply cost, quota, latency, and recency as routing utility signals or
135	   bounded power modifiers, not as silent replacements for capability.
136	6. Emit the resulting `power` and a compact `power_provenance` summary back into
137	   the catalog.
138	
139	Power should therefore answer "how strong is this model for automatic routing?"
140	Model × harness evidence should answer "how strong is this combination in this
141	benchmark environment?"
142	
143	## Derived Reports and Claim Grammar
144	
145	The ledger is successful only if it can produce strong, reproducible claims from
146	raw evidence. Reports should support two families of statements:
147	
148	1. Benchmark-specific comparative claims.
149	2. Cross-benchmark Fizeau Harness Intelligence claims.
150	
151	Example benchmark-specific claim:
152	
153	> fiz native with Opus 4.7 scores 81.0 on TerminalBench, 0.7 points below Claude
154	> Code with Opus 4.7 on the same subset.
155	
156	Example FHI claim:
157	
158	> Using fiz, the most effective model is Opus 4.7, with FHI 56.
159	
160	Example local-vs-frontier FHI claim:
161	
162	> With fiz 0.10 and oMLX 0.8.10, Qwen 3.6 27B 8-bit gets FHI 50, only 6
163	> points behind Opus 4.7.
164	
165	These claims require more than headline scores. A claim generator must include
166	or be able to trace:
167	
168	- exact Fizeau version or git commit
169	- exact harness name and harness version
170	- exact provider name, provider endpoint/API surface, and provider version or
171	  capture timestamp when no version is available
172	- exact model raw name, canonical model id when known, and resolved model
173	  snapshot/version when available
174	- deployment class, local runtime/server version, quantization, hardware
175	  profile, accelerator backend, context length, and reasoning/sampling controls
176	  for local or self-hosted stacks
177	- benchmark name, benchmark version, dataset commit, subset id/version, scorer,
178	  repetition count, and run timestamps
179	- score metric, normalized score, raw score, confidence interval or
180	  uncertainty note, and denominator
181	- invalid-run counts/classes and denominator handling
182	- source artifact paths and hashes, including session logs and upstream
183	  verifier outputs when available
184	
185	### Benchmark-Specific Claims
186	
187	Benchmark-specific reports compare rows only when the benchmark, scorer,
188	dataset/subset, model, and provider surface are intentionally controlled or when
189	the report states which axis is being varied.
190	
191	For example, a valid TerminalBench harness comparison may vary only
192	`subject.harness` while holding model/provider/benchmark/subset constant:
193	
194	```text
195	TerminalBench tb2-wide@<dataset_commit>, REPS=3
196	model=opus-4.7, provider=anthropic, benchmark=terminal-bench
197	
198	fiz-native       81.0 ± 2.1
199	claude-code      81.7 ± 1.8
200	delta            -0.7
201	```
202	
203	The report must not claim that a harness is better or worse when the rows also
204	vary model, provider, subset, scorer, or benchmark version unless the claim text
205	names those confounds explicitly.
206	
207	### FHI Claims
208	
209	Fizeau Harness Intelligence is a derived model × harness × provider metric. FHI
210	answers "how effective is this combination when driven through Fizeau's
211	execution surface?" It is separate from catalog model `power`, which answers
212	"how strong is this model for automatic routing?"
213	
214	An FHI report may rank models within a fixed harness/provider surface:
215	
216	```text
217	FHI for harness=fiz-native, provider=anthropic, evidence window=2026-Q2
218	
219	opus-4.7         56
220	sonnet-4.6       49
221	gpt-5.4-mini     43
222	```
223	
224	It may also rank harnesses within a fixed model/provider surface:
225	
226	```text
227	FHI for model=opus-4.7, provider=anthropic, evidence window=2026-Q2
228	
229	claude-code      57
230	fiz-native       56
231	fiz-claude       55
232	```
233	
234	FHI derivation is policy-owned and must be versioned. Every FHI output includes
235	the FHI formula version, benchmark weights, included evidence window, included
236	benchmarks, excluded evidence with reasons, and confidence/coverage notes.
237	
238	HumanEval, MMLU, and MHI-style components may contribute to FHI, but they must
239	not dominate long-horizon agentic evidence. TerminalBench, beadbench,
240	SkillsBench, and SWE-bench-style task outcomes should carry the primary weight
241	once enough harness-normalized rows exist.
242	
243	### Deployment-Class Comparisons
244	
245	FHI must support local-stack comparisons against frontier and non-frontier cloud
246	baselines. This is one of the primary product questions: whether local or
247	self-hosted deployments are close enough to frontier managed providers to be
248	useful under Fizeau.
249	
250	Example valid claim:
251	
252	```text
253	FHI formula=fhi/v1, evidence window=2026-Q2
254	benchmarks=terminalbench-wide, beadbench-v1, skillsbench-import
255	
256	local stack:
257	  fiz=0.10
258	  harness=fiz-native
259	  provider=omlx
260	  provider_version=0.8.10
261	  model=Qwen 3.6 27B MLX 8-bit
262	  quantization=8-bit
263	  hardware=Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512GB
264	
265	frontier baseline:
266	  harness=fiz-native
267	  provider=anthropic
268	  model=Opus 4.7
269	
270	Qwen 3.6 27B 8-bit via oMLX    FHI 50
271	Opus 4.7 via Anthropic          FHI 56
272	delta                           -6
273	```
274	
275	Deployment-class reports must group rows by at least:
276	
277	- `managed_frontier`
278	- `managed_non_frontier`
279	- `local`
280	- `self_hosted`
281	
282	Local/self-hosted rows require additional environment facts because those facts
283	are part of the capability surface:
284	
285	- runtime/server name and version, e.g. `omlx 0.8.10`
286	- model artifact id/path or checksum when available
287	- quantization and precision
288	- hardware class, memory, accelerator backend, and OS/architecture
289	- endpoint type, e.g. OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, native API
290	- context limit and reasoning/sampling controls actually applied
291	- utilization/capacity signals when available, such as active requests, queue
292	  depth, memory pressure, and tokens/s
293	
294	The claim generator must not compare a local row to a frontier row unless the
295	included benchmark set, scoring formula, evidence window, and denominator rules
296	are identical. If one side lacks a benchmark component, the report either
297	computes a coverage-adjusted FHI with an explicit confidence penalty or refuses
298	the comparison.
299	
300	## Initial Import Targets
301	
302	Near-term importers should cover:
303	
304	- `cmd/bench matrix` TerminalBench reports (`matrix.json`).
305	- Harbor job `result.json` and verifier reward files.
306	- beadbench `report.json`.
307	- public TerminalBench leaderboard reward cache.
308	- SkillsBench public rows or local SkillsBench reports.
309	- SWE-bench family leaderboard rows or task-level reports.
310	- HumanEval pass@k reports as low-cost coding/model-power components.
311	- MHI-style local eval reports when available.
312	
313	The first MHI-style source to support is Rapid-MLX commit
314	`903487e82ad1998f0c20b721a7df66ec815ea673`, documented in
315	`docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md`.
316	
317	Benchmark-specific resource notes:
318	
319	- `docs/resources/skillsbench-2026-05-06.md`
320	- `docs/resources/swebench-2026-05-06.md`
321	- `docs/resources/humaneval-2026-05-06.md`
322	
323	Each importer should preserve source artifact paths and source hashes so a
324	ledger record can be traced back to the original run.
325	
326	## Storage Policy
327	
328	Raw benchmark output directories remain gitignored under `benchmark-results/`.
329	They may contain large logs, model outputs, tarballs, local auth-derived paths,
330	or upstream artifacts that should not be committed.
331	
332	Curated evidence is stored separately:
333	
334	- Local working ledgers: `benchmark-results/evidence/<run-id>.jsonl`.
335	- Checked-in small fixtures: `scripts/benchmark/testdata/evidence/`.
336	- Checked-in curated snapshots, when explicitly approved:
337	  `scripts/benchmark/evidence/<snapshot-id>.jsonl`.
338	- Human-readable summaries and claims: `docs/research/`.
339	
340	Checked-in curated snapshots must contain normalized evidence records only, not
341	raw prompts, raw tool outputs, credentials, or large upstream artifacts. Every
342	record in a checked-in snapshot must include source artifact hashes or URLs so
343	the raw source can be audited outside git.
344	
345	## Implementation Beads
346	
347	The implementation work for this design is tracked under DDx epic
348	`fizeau-89e1e403` ("EPIC: Build FHI benchmark evidence pipeline"). Child beads
349	must stay scoped to one implementation layer each:
350	
351	1. `fizeau-39b9669a` — extend and validate
352	   `benchmark-evidence.schema.json` for versioned axes, local-runtime metadata,
353	   session-log provenance, and invalid-run classes.
354	2. `fizeau-395d124d` — implement a ledger writer/importer CLI for appending
355	   validated JSONL records.
356	3. `fizeau-2c59b948` — import TerminalBench matrix outputs and link Fizeau
357	   session logs and Harbor verifier artifacts.
358	4. `fizeau-fde8c9bd` — import beadbench reports and DDx execute-bead evidence.
359	5. `fizeau-ff5fcc61` — import external benchmark rows/reports for Rapid-MLX
360	   MHI, SkillsBench, SWE-bench, and HumanEval.
361	6. `fizeau-d5e91885` — implement a versioned FHI formula and claim generator.
362	7. `fizeau-dcb621f8` — document one reproducible workflow from benchmark
363	   execution to ledger import to FHI/claim output.
364	
365	Each child bead must name its in-scope files, out-of-scope files, and at least
366	one command-based acceptance criterion.
367	
368	## Open Questions
369	
370	- Exact power derivation weights. These should be data-driven once we have
371	  enough harness-normalized TerminalBench and local-model runs.
372	- Whether latency/cost should affect catalog `power` directly or only routing
373	  score. The current default should be conservative: keep power capability-led
374	  and use routing score for cost/latency preference.

8	
9	# Solution Design: SD-012 — Benchmark Evidence Ledger and Derived Model Power
10	
11	## Summary
12	
13	Fizeau should treat benchmark observations as raw evidence, not as direct
14	catalog truth. Every benchmark runner should be able to emit normalized records
15	keyed by:
16	
17	- model
18	- harness
19	- provider
20	- benchmark
21	- benchmark task or subset
22	- run environment and scoring metadata
23	
24	Catalog `power` then becomes a derived projection over those records plus
25	cost, availability, recency, deployment class, and explicit override policy.
26	This preserves the distinction between model capability and model × harness ×
27	provider compatibility while still letting benchmark performance drive routing
28	strength over time.
29	
30	## Problem
31	
32	TerminalBench, MHI-style evals, SkillsBench, SWE-bench, HumanEval, MMLU,
33	TAU-bench, and project-local beadbench results all measure different things.
34	The concrete MHI source captured for this design is Rapid-MLX's Model-Harness
35	Index resource in `docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md`; SkillsBench,
36	SWE-bench, and HumanEval are captured in sibling files under `docs/resources/`.
37	Some benchmarks are close to model-only capability. Others are explicitly model
38	× harness behavior. Current Fizeau catalog power stores a single integer with
39	provenance, but the raw evidence that led to the integer is not represented in a
40	common shape.
41	
42	Without a raw evidence layer:
43	
44	- TerminalBench leaderboard rows can be misread as model-only scores even when
45	  the row is really `Harness__Model`.
46	- Harness effects such as tool-call parsing, prompt discipline, retry behavior,
47	  and session logging get folded into model power without attribution.
48	- Cost, speed, quota, and availability signals are mixed with capability
49	  judgments in ad hoc ways.
50	- Recomputing model power after new benchmark runs requires reconstructing
51	  intent from benchmark-specific report files.
52	
53	## Decision
54	
55	Introduce a benchmark evidence ledger format. Existing benchmark-specific
56	outputs remain the source artifacts, but importers can project them into a
57	shared JSONL record type described by
58	`scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json`.
59	
60	The ledger is append-only evidence. It does not directly change routing.
61	Catalog generation or catalog-refresh tooling reads the ledger and computes
62	model-level derived power plus model × harness capability summaries.
63	
64	## Record Identity
65	
66	A single evidence record represents one aggregate or one atomic trial. Atomic
67	task-level records are preferred when available; aggregate records are allowed
68	when the upstream source only publishes aggregate scores.
69	
70	Identity fields:
71	
72	- `schema_version`: evidence schema version.
73	- `record_id`: stable content-derived identifier.
74	- `captured_at`: when Fizeau captured/imported the record.
75	- `source`: source runner or external publisher.
76	- `benchmark`: benchmark identity and version.
77	- `subject`: model, harness, provider, endpoint, and optional surface.
78	- `scope`: task, subset, split, repetition, and run identifiers.
79	
80	Versioned identity is required for evidence that may feed FHI, catalog power,
81	or comparative claims. Records must capture, directly or through provenance:
82	
83	- Fizeau version and git commit.
84	- Harness wrapper name/version and wrapped harness CLI/runtime version.
85	- Provider name, endpoint/API surface, deployment class, and provider version or
86	  capture timestamp.
87	- Model raw name, canonical catalog id when known, resolved snapshot/version
88	  when available, quantization/precision for local artifacts, and context limit.
89	- Benchmark name/version, scorer version, dataset commit, subset id/version, and
90	  runner/importer version.
91	- Local/self-hosted runtime version, model artifact id/checksum, OS/architecture,
92	  hardware class, accelerator backend, and utilization/capacity signals when
93	  available.
94	
95	## Subject Semantics
96	
97	`subject.model` is the canonical model identity if known. `subject.model_raw`
98	preserves the model string from the source. `subject.harness` and
99	`subject.provider` are never optional for agentic/tool benchmarks; if a public
100	source hides either value, it must be recorded as `unknown`, not omitted.
101	
102	This prevents the common mistake of treating `ClaudeCode__GLM-4.7` as a GLM-only
103	score. It is a score for GLM-4.7 through Claude Code, on whatever provider and
104	version the source used.
105	
106	## Score Semantics
107	
108	The normalized `score` block carries the headline metric in a common form:
109	
110	- `metric`: e.g. `pass_rate`, `reward_mean`, `accuracy`, `mhi`.
111	- `value`: normalized 0..1 score when possible.
112	- `raw_value`: original score if different, e.g. `92` for MHI on a 0..100 scale.
113	- `n`: number of trials or tasks represented.
114	- `passed`: count of passed trials when applicable.
115	- `failed`: count of failed trials when applicable.
116	
117	Additional benchmark-specific dimensions live under `components`; examples:
118	`tool_call_success`, `terminalbench_pass_rate`, `humaneval_pass_rate`,
119	`mmlu_accuracy`, `median_wall_seconds`, `tool_calls_per_success`, and
120	`cost_per_success_usd`.
121	
122	## Derived Power
123	
124	Catalog `models.yaml` remains the compact routing surface. `power` is derived
125	from evidence, but the derivation is intentionally policy-owned:
126	
127	1. Normalize each benchmark into capability dimensions.
128	2. Separate model-only evidence from model × harness evidence.
129	3. Weight reliable, harness-normalized agentic benchmarks heavily for coding
130	   agent routing. TerminalBench should become a major contributor once we have
131	   harness-normalized rows.
132	4. Apply deployment-class and availability guardrails. A local/community model
133	   should not receive managed-cloud frontier power from one benchmark alone.
134	5. Apply cost, quota, latency, and recency as routing utility signals or
135	   bounded power modifiers, not as silent replacements for capability.
136	6. Emit the resulting `power` and a compact `power_provenance` summary back into
137	   the catalog.
138	
139	Power should therefore answer "how strong is this model for automatic routing?"
140	Model × harness evidence should answer "how strong is this combination in this
141	benchmark environment?"
142	
143	## Derived Reports and Claim Grammar
144	
145	The ledger is successful only if it can produce strong, reproducible claims from
146	raw evidence. Reports should support two families of statements:
147	
148	1. Benchmark-specific comparative claims.
149	2. Cross-benchmark Fizeau Harness Intelligence claims.
150	
151	Example benchmark-specific claim:
152	
153	> fiz native with Opus 4.7 scores 81.0 on TerminalBench, 0.7 points below Claude
154	> Code with Opus 4.7 on the same subset.
155	
156	Example FHI claim:
157	
158	> Using fiz, the most effective model is Opus 4.7, with FHI 56.
159	
160	Example local-vs-frontier FHI claim:
161	
162	> With fiz 0.10 and oMLX 0.8.10, Qwen 3.6 27B 8-bit gets FHI 50, only 6
163	> points behind Opus 4.7.
164	
165	These claims require more than headline scores. A claim generator must include
166	or be able to trace:
167	
168	- exact Fizeau version or git commit
169	- exact harness name and harness version
170	- exact provider name, provider endpoint/API surface, and provider version or
171	  capture timestamp when no version is available
172	- exact model raw name, canonical model id when known, and resolved model
173	  snapshot/version when available
174	- deployment class, local runtime/server version, quantization, hardware
175	  profile, accelerator backend, context length, and reasoning/sampling controls
176	  for local or self-hosted stacks
177	- benchmark name, benchmark version, dataset commit, subset id/version, scorer,
178	  repetition count, and run timestamps
179	- score metric, normalized score, raw score, confidence interval or
180	  uncertainty note, and denominator
181	- invalid-run counts/classes and denominator handling
182	- source artifact paths and hashes, including session logs and upstream
183	  verifier outputs when available
184	
185	### Benchmark-Specific Claims
186	
187	Benchmark-specific reports compare rows only when the benchmark, scorer,
188	dataset/subset, model, and provider surface are intentionally controlled or when
189	the report states which axis is being varied.
190	
191	For example, a valid TerminalBench harness comparison may vary only
192	`subject.harness` while holding model/provider/benchmark/subset constant:
193	
194	```text
195	TerminalBench tb2-wide@<dataset_commit>, REPS=3
196	model=opus-4.7, provider=anthropic, benchmark=terminal-bench
197	
198	fiz-native       81.0 ± 2.1
199	claude-code      81.7 ± 1.8
200	delta            -0.7
201	```
202	
203	The report must not claim that a harness is better or worse when the rows also
204	vary model, provider, subset, scorer, or benchmark version unless the claim text
205	names those confounds explicitly.
206	
207	### FHI Claims
208	
209	Fizeau Harness Intelligence is a derived model × harness × provider metric. FHI
210	answers "how effective is this combination when driven through Fizeau's
211	execution surface?" It is separate from catalog model `power`, which answers
212	"how strong is this model for automatic routing?"
213	
214	An FHI report may rank models within a fixed harness/provider surface:
215	
216	```text
217	FHI for harness=fiz-native, provider=anthropic, evidence window=2026-Q2
218	
219	opus-4.7         56
220	sonnet-4.6       49
221	gpt-5.4-mini     43
222	```
223	
224	It may also rank harnesses within a fixed model/provider surface:
225	
226	```text
227	FHI for model=opus-4.7, provider=anthropic, evidence window=2026-Q2
228	
229	claude-code      57
230	fiz-native       56
231	fiz-claude       55
232	```
233	
234	FHI derivation is policy-owned and must be versioned. Every FHI output includes
235	the FHI formula version, benchmark weights, included evidence window, included
236	benchmarks, excluded evidence with reasons, and confidence/coverage notes.
237	
238	HumanEval, MMLU, and MHI-style components may contribute to FHI, but they must
239	not dominate long-horizon agentic evidence. TerminalBench, beadbench,
240	SkillsBench, and SWE-bench-style task outcomes should carry the primary weight
241	once enough harness-normalized rows exist.
242	
243	### Deployment-Class Comparisons
244	
245	FHI must support local-stack comparisons against frontier and non-frontier cloud
246	baselines. This is one of the primary product questions: whether local or
247	self-hosted deployments are close enough to frontier managed providers to be
248	useful under Fizeau.
249	
250	Example valid claim:
251	
252	```text
253	FHI formula=fhi/v1, evidence window=2026-Q2
254	benchmarks=terminalbench-wide, beadbench-v1, skillsbench-import
255	
256	local stack:
257	  fiz=0.10
258	  harness=fiz-native
259	  provider=omlx
260	  provider_version=0.8.10
261	  model=Qwen 3.6 27B MLX 8-bit
262	  quantization=8-bit
263	  hardware=Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512GB
264	
265	frontier baseline:
266	  harness=fiz-native
267	  provider=anthropic
268	  model=Opus 4.7
269	
270	Qwen 3.6 27B 8-bit via oMLX    FHI 50
271	Opus 4.7 via Anthropic          FHI 56
272	delta                           -6
273	```
274	
275	Deployment-class reports must group rows by at least:
276	
277	- `managed_frontier`
278	- `managed_non_frontier`
279	- `local`
280	- `self_hosted`
281	
282	Local/self-hosted rows require additional environment facts because those facts
283	are part of the capability surface:
284	
285	- runtime/server name and version, e.g. `omlx 0.8.10`
286	- model artifact id/path or checksum when available
287	- quantization and precision
288	- hardware class, memory, accelerator backend, and OS/architecture
289	- endpoint type, e.g. OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, native API
290	- context limit and reasoning/sampling controls actually applied
291	- utilization/capacity signals when available, such as active requests, queue
292	  depth, memory pressure, and tokens/s
293	
294	The claim generator must not compare a local row to a frontier row unless the
295	included benchmark set, scoring formula, evidence window, and denominator rules
296	are identical. If one side lacks a benchmark component, the report either
297	computes a coverage-adjusted FHI with an explicit confidence penalty or refuses
298	the comparison.
299	
300	## Initial Import Targets
301	
302	Near-term importers should cover:
303	
304	- `cmd/bench matrix` TerminalBench reports (`matrix.json`).
305	- Harbor job `result.json` and verifier reward files.
306	- beadbench `report.json`.
307	- public TerminalBench leaderboard reward cache.
308	- SkillsBench public rows or local SkillsBench reports.
309	- SWE-bench family leaderboard rows or task-level reports.
310	- HumanEval pass@k reports as low-cost coding/model-power components.
311	- MHI-style local eval reports when available.
312	
313	The first MHI-style source to support is Rapid-MLX commit
314	`903487e82ad1998f0c20b721a7df66ec815ea673`, documented in
315	`docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md`.
316	
317	Benchmark-specific resource notes:
318	
319	- `docs/resources/skillsbench-2026-05-06.md`
320	- `docs/resources/swebench-2026-05-06.md`
321	- `docs/resources/humaneval-2026-05-06.md`
322	
323	Each importer should preserve source artifact paths and source hashes so a
324	ledger record can be traced back to the original run.
325	
326	## Storage Policy
327	
328	Raw benchmark output directories remain gitignored under `benchmark-results/`.
329	They may contain large logs, model outputs, tarballs, local auth-derived paths,
330	or upstream artifacts that should not be committed.
331	
332	Curated evidence is stored separately:
333	
334	- Local working ledgers: `benchmark-results/evidence/<run-id>.jsonl`.
335	- Checked-in small fixtures: `scripts/benchmark/testdata/evidence/`.
336	- Checked-in curated snapshots, when explicitly approved:
337	  `scripts/benchmark/evidence/<snapshot-id>.jsonl`.
338	- Human-readable summaries and claims: `docs/research/`.
339	
340	Checked-in curated snapshots must contain normalized evidence records only, not
341	raw prompts, raw tool outputs, credentials, or large upstream artifacts. Every
342	record in a checked-in snapshot must include source artifact hashes or URLs so
343	the raw source can be audited outside git.
344	
345	## Implementation Beads
346	
347	The implementation work for this design is tracked under DDx epic
348	`fizeau-89e1e403` ("EPIC: Build FHI benchmark evidence pipeline"). Child beads
349	must stay scoped to one implementation layer each:
350	
351	1. `fizeau-39b9669a` — extend and validate
352	   `benchmark-evidence.schema.json` for versioned axes, local-runtime metadata,
353	   session-log provenance, and invalid-run classes.
354	2. `fizeau-395d124d` — implement a ledger writer/importer CLI for appending
355	   validated JSONL records.
356	3. `fizeau-2c59b948` — import TerminalBench matrix outputs and link Fizeau
357	   session logs and Harbor verifier artifacts.
358	4. `fizeau-fde8c9bd` — import beadbench reports and DDx execute-bead evidence.
359	5. `fizeau-ff5fcc61` — import external benchmark rows/reports for Rapid-MLX
360	   MHI, SkillsBench, SWE-bench, and HumanEval.
361	6. `fizeau-d5e91885` — implement a versioned FHI formula and claim generator.
362	7. `fizeau-dcb621f8` — document one reproducible workflow from benchmark
363	   execution to ledger import to FHI/claim output.
364	
365	Each child bead must name its in-scope files, out-of-scope files, and at least
366	one command-based acceptance criterion.
367	
368	## Open Questions
369	
370	- Exact power derivation weights. These should be data-driven once we have
371	  enough harness-normalized TerminalBench and local-model runs.
372	- Whether latency/cost should affect catalog `power` directly or only routing
373	  score. The current default should be conservative: keep power capability-led
374	  and use routing score for cost/latency preference.
